data.content_ref: inline:The target's own countercondition #1 states that the defense fails if 'the preference implies any increase in subjective probability or rational expectation of future success.' Yet the target's mechanism explicitly describes the preference as 'a bet on the currently fittest survivor.' The ordinary meaning of a 'bet' entails an expectation that the chosen option will outperform alternatives — one does not bet on something while disclaiming any expectation of its success. By characterizing the pragmatic rule as a 'bet,' the target has already conceded the very condition it sets out to avoid: a bet on the fittest survivor is intelligible only if the bettor has some expectation that past fitness tracks future performance, which is exactly the rational expectation of future success that countercondition #1 forbids. The defense is therefore self-defeating: its own mechanism language violates its own stated countercondition.
